LD operations

Source: vignettes/ld.Rmd
ld.Rmd

Linkage disequilibrium (LD) is how strongly two variants are inherited together, measured by their correlation r. opengwasr reads LD from LD Stores on the OpenGWAS API, or from your own PLINK Reference. This vignette covers each LD operation: choosing the LD, LD matrices, LD proxies, reflookup and clumping.

Variants are named by ALID, as everywhere in opengwasr (see ALIDs). The sign of r refers to the first allele in each ALID.

Status. Every chunk runs, replayed from responses recorded against the development Data API on 23 November 2026, except the PLINK Reference section, which is shown but not evaluated: building the vignette would need a PLINK binary and a genotype fileset such as 1000 Genomes, which CRAN doesn’t have. Its grey output blocks marked # illustrative are shaped the way opengwasr returns them (the API isn’t involved in them). The package’s tests run the same functions with PLINK on a small committed fileset wherever a PLINK binary can be found, as in CI; elsewhere they are skipped.

Developer note: The API responses in this vignette were recorded against the development Data API, directly, with a developer key (see vignettes/recordings.R). Once the OpenGWAS Gateway is live (#18), re-record through it, so the vignettes show the access users will have.

library(opengwasr)
src <- og_api()

LD Stores

An LD Store holds the LD of one reference panel of one ancestry, on GRCh38. og_ld_stores() lists them:

og_ld_stores(src)
##              ld_store ancestry   n      t_far near_bp   far_bp n_variants
## 1 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10      EUR 665 0.03186544 3000000 10000000    8586889
## 2 hgdp1kgp-v2-AFR-k10      AFR 608 0.03490787 3000000 10000000   14374341
## 3 hgdp1kgp-v2-EAS-k10      EAS 724 0.02922861 3000000 10000000    7837854
## 4 hgdp1kgp-v2-SAS-k10      SAS 672 0.03152799 3000000 10000000    8879035
## 5 hgdp1kgp-v2-AMR-k10      AMR 341 0.06315152 3000000 10000000    7561067
##   default ready
## 1      NA  TRUE
## 2      NA  TRUE
## 3      NA  TRUE
## 4      NA  TRUE
## 5      NA  TRUE
  • n is the number of people whose genotypes the LD Store was built from (HGDP + 1000 Genomes).
  • An LD Store doesn’t hold every pair of variants. Within near_bp (3 Mb) of each other, it holds every pair’s r. From near_bp to far_bp (10 Mb), it holds r only for pairs whose r² reaches its Far Threshold, t_far; for the rest it knows only that r² is below t_far. Beyond far_bp, and across chromosomes, it holds nothing.
  • A variant the LD Store doesn’t cover is absent from it. Every LD operation tells you how many variants were absent.
  • default will mark each ancestry’s default LD Store once the API declares one. Until then it is NA.

Choosing the LD

Matching by Assigned Ancestry

By default, opengwasr uses the LD Store that matches each Analysis’s Assigned Ancestry, the ancestry opengwasdb inferred from the Analysis’s allele frequencies. Analyses of different ancestries in one call each get their own LD Store. Here, two Analyses’ top hits are clumped (see Clumping):

both <- og_tophits(src, c("OGS-00011:GCST003116", "OGS-00013:GCST90475090"))
unique(both[, c("id", "clump_ld", "clump_ld_choice", "clump_r2", "clump_kb")])
##                        id            clump_ld clump_ld_choice   clump_r2
## 1    OGS-00011:GCST003116 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10         matched 0.03186544
## 50 OGS-00013:GCST90475090 hgdp1kgp-v2-AFR-k10         matched 0.03490787
##    clump_kb
## 1     10000
## 50    10000

OGS-00013:GCST90475090 (HbA1c, Assigned Ancestry AFR) is clumped against African LD, at that LD Store’s own t_far. A non-European Analysis is never given European LD unless you ask for it. An LD matrix or LD proxies of a data frame of Associations choose the same way, from its id column, and og_provenance() records the choice in ld and ld_choice.

If several LD Stores serve one ancestry, opengwasr uses the one the LD Store list declares as that ancestry’s default, and clump_ld_choice (or ld_choice) says "ancestry_default". Today each ancestry has one LD Store. (og_ld_stores()’s default column says which; it is NA until the API declares one, and an ancestry with several LD Stores and no declared default is refused.)

The ld argument

og_tophits(), og_clump(), og_ld_matrix() and og_ld_proxies() all take ld, and it means the same in each:

ld LD used
NULL (default) The LD Store matching each Analysis’s Assigned Ancestry
An LD Store’s name, such as "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10" That LD Store
An ancestry, such as "EUR" That ancestry’s LD Store (its declared default, if it has several)
og_plink_reference(path) Your own PLINK Reference, on your machine (below)

An exact LD Store name wins; otherwise ld is read as an ancestry code and resolved to that ancestry’s LD Store. LD Store names (hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10) and ancestry codes (EUR, AFR, EAS, SAS, AMR) can’t be confused today, and the provenance always records which LD Store was used. A name gives ld_choice = "user" (clump_ld_choice when clumping); an ancestry code gives "ancestry_default".

ld is separate from the Source the Associations come from, so the same LD choice keeps working whichever Source you use.

cad_eur <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", ld = "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10")
## Warning in og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", ld = "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10"):
## 234 of the 2,194 top hits of OGS-00011:GCST003116 aren't in LD Store
## hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10, so they can't be clumped and were left out.
unique(cad_eur$clump_ld_choice)
## [1] "user"

A plain vector of variants has no ancestry to match, so og_ld_matrix() and og_ld_proxies() need ld when given one.

Unassigned and mixed ancestry

An Analysis whose allele frequencies match no single ancestry confidently is Unassigned (assigned_ancestry is NA in og_analyses()). opengwasr won’t guess an LD Store for it, and never falls back to European LD:

og_tophits(src, "OGS-00014:GCST90475125")
## Error in `og_tophits()`:
## ! Can't choose an LD Store for OGS-00014:GCST90475125: its ancestry is Unassigned.
## ℹ Its allele frequencies match no single ancestry confidently.
## ℹ Choose the LD with `ld`, from: "EUR", "AFR", "EAS", "SAS", "AMR" (see `og_ld_stores()`).
## ℹ Or pass `clump = FALSE` for unclumped top hits.

The error has class opengwasr_ld_unmatched, a kind of opengwasr_refusal, with the LD Stores in e$ld_stores. If you decide AMR LD is right for it (its source describes it as “AMR”), say so:

basophils <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00014:GCST90475125", ld = "AMR")
unique(basophils$clump_ld)
## [1] "hgdp1kgp-v2-AMR-k10"

The same refusal applies whenever one LD Store is needed for several Analyses (an LD matrix, or og_clump()), and their ancestries differ or one of them is Unassigned. One LD Store is never applied to a different ancestry without your say-so.

LD matrices

og_ld_matrix() returns the signed LD correlation r between every pair of variants:

m <- og_ld_matrix(
  src,
  c("16:53772541:A:G", "16:53767042:C:T", "18:60161902:C:T", "2:628504:A:G", "5:75701728:A:AAAAT"),
  ld = "EUR"
)
round(m, 3)
##                    16:53772541:A:G 16:53767042:C:T 18:60161902:C:T 2:628504:A:G
## 16:53772541:A:G              1.000          -0.998              NA           NA
## 16:53767042:C:T             -0.998           1.000              NA           NA
## 18:60161902:C:T                 NA              NA               1           NA
## 2:628504:A:G                    NA              NA              NA            1
## 5:75701728:A:AAAAT              NA              NA              NA           NA
##                    5:75701728:A:AAAAT
## 16:53772541:A:G                    NA
## 16:53767042:C:T                    NA
## 18:60161902:C:T                    NA
## 2:628504:A:G                       NA
## 5:75701728:A:AAAAT                  1
  • The dimension names are ALIDs. The sign of r refers to the first allele in each name. Square it for r².
  • Variants can be rsIDs or ALIDs. rsIDs are translated to ALIDs first, and every ALID of an rsID is included.
  • Absent variants are left out of the matrix, with a warning giving how many; og_provenance(m)$absent lists them.
  • More than 500 variants are split into several Jobs, and the pieces are put back together so that every pair is included.

Given a data frame of Associations, og_ld_matrix() matches the LD Store by the Analyses’ Assigned Ancestry:

cad <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
m <- og_ld_matrix(src, cad)
og_provenance(m)$ld
## [1] "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10"

Missing pairs, and filling them with 0

A pair the LD Store doesn’t hold is NA, never 0 by default. NA means one of two things:

  • Below the Far Threshold. The two variants are on one chromosome, between near_bp and far_bp apart, and their r² is below t_far. The LD Store knows they are at most weakly linked (for EUR, |r| below about 0.18), but not r itself.
  • Not measured. The two variants are more than far_bp apart, or on different chromosomes. The LD Store holds nothing about them.

Many methods need a number for every pair. fill_below_t_far = TRUE sets the first kind to 0 and leaves the second NA:

v <- c("7:105919152:C:T", "7:105920689:A:G", "7:110998200:C:T", "7:117559403:A:G", "16:53767042:C:T")
round(og_ld_matrix(src, v, ld = "EUR"), 3)
##                 7:105919152:C:T 7:105920689:A:G 7:110998200:C:T 7:117559403:A:G
## 7:105919152:C:T           1.000          -0.182              NA              NA
## 7:105920689:A:G          -0.182           1.000              NA              NA
## 7:110998200:C:T              NA              NA               1              NA
## 7:117559403:A:G              NA              NA              NA               1
## 16:53767042:C:T              NA              NA              NA              NA
##                 16:53767042:C:T
## 7:105919152:C:T              NA
## 7:105920689:A:G              NA
## 7:110998200:C:T              NA
## 7:117559403:A:G              NA
## 16:53767042:C:T               1
round(og_ld_matrix(src, v, ld = "EUR", fill_below_t_far = TRUE), 3)
##                 7:105919152:C:T 7:105920689:A:G 7:110998200:C:T 7:117559403:A:G
## 7:105919152:C:T           1.000          -0.182               0              NA
## 7:105920689:A:G          -0.182           1.000               0              NA
## 7:110998200:C:T           0.000           0.000               1               0
## 7:117559403:A:G              NA              NA               0               1
## 16:53767042:C:T              NA              NA              NA              NA
##                 16:53767042:C:T
## 7:105919152:C:T              NA
## 7:105920689:A:G              NA
## 7:110998200:C:T              NA
## 7:117559403:A:G              NA
## 16:53767042:C:T               1

7:110998200:C:T is about 5 Mb from the first two variants and 6.6 Mb from 7:117559403:A:G: inside the far window, so those pairs become 0. The first two variants are 11.6 Mb from 7:117559403:A:G, beyond far_bp, so those pairs stay NA, as do all pairs with the chromosome 16 variant.

The option is off by default because 0 claims more than the LD Store knows: only that r² is below t_far. Within near_bp nothing is missing, so it changes nothing there. A matrix from a PLINK Reference has every pair, so the option doesn’t apply.

LD proxies

og_ld_proxies() finds the variants in LD with each variant you give: every variant within kb kilobases whose r² with it is at least r2 (defaults 0.8 and 10,000 kb). Strongest first:

px <- og_ld_proxies(src, "16:53767042:C:T", ld = "EUR")
nrow(px)
## [1] 98
head(px, 5)
##              alid      proxy_alid          r        r2 distance
## 1 16:53767042:C:T 16:53768582:C:T -1.0000000 1.0000000     1540
## 2 16:53767042:C:T 16:53769311:A:G  1.0000000 1.0000000     2269
## 3 16:53767042:C:T 16:53769662:A:T  1.0000000 1.0000000     2620
## 4 16:53767042:C:T 16:53775211:C:T -1.0000000 1.0000000     8169
## 5 16:53767042:C:T 16:53772541:A:G -0.9980431 0.9960899     5499
  • r is signed for the first alleles of alid and proxy_alid; distance is in base pairs.
  • Variants can be rsIDs or ALIDs, or a data frame of Associations, whose Analyses’ Assigned Ancestry then chooses the LD Store.
  • Absent variants have no LD proxies, and a warning (class opengwasr_ld_absent_variants) gives how many.
  • r2 and kb follow the same rule as clumping: below t_far, kb can be at most 3,000 (Your own r² and window). Otherwise the API refuses (opengwasr_ld_refusal, with reason, t_far, near_bp and far_bp).

This is an LD lookup, for questions about LD itself: which variants tag a signal, or which variants to look for in data from outside OpenGWAS. It is not the LD-proxy substitution ieugwasr made when an outcome lacked a variant. opengwasr never swaps another variant’s Association in for a missing one; Reference-Completed Store Releases hold Imputed Associations instead (see Imputed Associations).

Is a variant in the LD Store?

og_ld_reflookup() says whether the LD Store holds each variant, so you can check instruments before clumping or building an LD matrix. It returns one row per variant asked, with alid, rsid (when known) and present:

og_ld_reflookup(src, c("16:53767042:C:T", "rs1421085", "16:53767042:A:C"), ld = "EUR")
##              alid      rsid present
## 1 16:53767042:C:T      <NA>    TRUE
## 2 16:53767042:C:T rs1421085    TRUE
## 3 16:53767042:A:G rs1421085   FALSE
## 4 16:53767042:A:C      <NA>   FALSE
  • An rsID stands for every ALID it names, one row each: rs1421085 names two ALIDs here, and the LD Store holds one of them. An rsID no GWAS Store holds has one row with alid NA and present FALSE.
  • A variant the LD Store doesn’t hold is a row, not a warning; og_provenance() lists them as absent.
  • ld is chosen as for the other LD functions, and only an LD Store can answer: a PLINK Reference is refused.

Clumping

Clumping keeps one variant per independent signal.

Top hits are clumped by default

og_tophits() clumps unless you pass clump = FALSE:

cad <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
## Warning in og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116"): 234 of the 2,194 top hits
## of OGS-00011:GCST003116 aren't in LD Store hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10, so they can't
## be clumped and were left out.
nrow(cad)
## [1] 49
head(cad[, c("rsid", "alid", "beta", "pval", "clump_size")], 5)
##          rsid            alid        beta         pval clump_size
## 1   rs2891168  9:22098620:A:G -0.19335911 2.296241e-98        193
## 2  rs55730499 6:160584578:C:T -0.31671619 5.392728e-39         94
## 3   rs7528419 1:109274570:A:G  0.11453085 1.968746e-23          9
## 4   rs4711863  6:12915185:C:G -0.09856474 1.613590e-21         96
## 5 rs115654617 2:203029276:A:C  0.13790739 3.119371e-18        316

The 2,194 top hits at p ≤ 5e-8 reduce to 49 index variants. clump_size counts the top hits each index variant stands for, itself included.

  • Variants are ranked by |z|. Starting from the strongest, each index variant absorbs every weaker top hit within kb kilobases whose r² with it is above r2 (the rule plink --clump uses).
  • Every top hit at the threshold is clumped, and limit (default 1,000) then caps the index variants returned.
  • Absent top hits can’t be clumped. They are left out, with a warning giving how many, and the count is kept in the provenance.

Default thresholds come from the LD Store

You don’t need to choose r2 and kb. By default, opengwasr clumps within the LD Store’s far window (10,000 kb), at its Far Threshold t_far (about 0.03). That is always a question the LD Store can answer exactly.

ieugwasr’s default, r² 0.001 within 10,000 kb, is not. Beyond 3,000 kb an LD Store keeps only pairs with r² ≥ t_far, so it can’t tell an r² of 0.001 from one of 0.02 there. If you ask for it, opengwasr refuses.

Your own r² and window, and reading a refusal

Pass r2 and kb to clump with your own thresholds. If the LD Store can answer them exactly, it does. If not, the API refuses and says why, and opengwasr passes its message on. It never clumps at something close to what you asked.

og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000)
## Error in `og_tophits()`:
## ! r2=0.001 is below t_far=0.03186544342507645: beyond 3,000,000 bp the store holds only the Bound r² < t_far for unstored pairs, which does not decide r̂² ≥ r2

The message is the API’s. The error has class opengwasr_ld_refusal, a kind of opengwasr_refusal. It carries the API’s reason and the LD Store’s limits as fields, so a script can decide what to do: here, any r2 is answered within near_bp, 3,000 kb, and an r2 of at least t_far within far_bp, 10,000 kb. Catch opengwasr_ld_refusal itself to read those fields; the parent class opengwasr_refusal also covers refusals that don’t have them:

cad_strict <- tryCatch(
  og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000),
  opengwasr_ld_refusal = function(e) {
    message("Refused (", e$reason, "); clumping within ", e$near_bp / 1000, " kb instead.")
    og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", r2 = 0.001, kb = e$near_bp / 1000)
  }
)
## Refused (threshold_below_t_far); clumping within 3000 kb instead.

Fields, as the API sends them: e$reason (here "threshold_below_t_far"), e$store (the LD Store), e$ancestry, e$t_far, e$near_bp and e$far_bp. og_ld_proxies() refuses in the same way.

Clumping data you already have

og_clump() clumps any data frame of Associations as one set, such as the top hits of several Analyses together. It needs alid and z, and an id column if the LD Store is to be matched by ancestry. A variant listed several times is ranked by its largest |z|, and every Association of a kept variant is returned. Here the 100 strongest index variants of each Analysis are clumped together:

bmi <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST90029007", limit = 100)
ldl <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST90002412", limit = 100)
joint <- og_clump(src, rbind(bmi, ldl))
table(joint$id)
## 
## OGS-00011:GCST90002412 OGS-00011:GCST90029007 
##                    100                     97

og_clump() takes ld, r2 and kb exactly as og_tophits() does. With the default ld = NULL, every Analysis in data must share one Assigned Ancestry:

hba1c_afr <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00013:GCST90475090", limit = 100)
og_clump(src, rbind(bmi, hba1c_afr))
## Error in `og_clump()`:
## ! Can't choose one LD Store for these Analyses: their Assigned Ancestries differ.
## • AFR: OGS-00013:GCST90475090
## • EUR: OGS-00011:GCST90029007
## ℹ Choose the LD with `ld`, from: "EUR", "AFR", "EAS", "SAS", "AMR" (see `og_ld_stores()`).

A data frame with no id column has no Assigned Ancestry to match, so ld must be given.

Clumping provenance

Every clumped data frame records how it was clumped, in columns that survive subsetting, merging and binding:

Column Meaning
clump_ld The LD Store’s name, or the PLINK Reference’s path
clump_ld_choice How it was chosen: "matched" (the one LD Store for the Analysis’s Assigned Ancestry), "ancestry_default" (an ancestry’s default LD Store: you passed an ancestry code in ld, or the Assigned Ancestry has several LD Stores) or "user" (you named an LD Store or a PLINK Reference in ld)
clump_r2, clump_kb The r² and window applied, whether defaults or yours
clump_size How many top hits the index variant stands for

og_provenance() (defined in Getting started) adds the counts behind them. Unlike the columns, it doesn’t survive rbind():

og_provenance(cad)
## ── opengwasr provenance ─────────────────
## • Query: og_tophits(threshold = 5e-08, limit = 1000, observed_only = FALSE, clump = TRUE, original_units = FALSE)
## • Store Releases: OGS-00011/OGS-00011-completed
## • Clumped: OGS-00011:GCST003116 in hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10 (matched), r² 0.0319 within 10,000 kb; 2,194 top hits, 234 not in the LD Store, 49 index variants
## • Jobs: 86d6e51a
## • Rows: 49 returned of 49 matching
## • Retrieved: 2026-11-24 14:04:33 UTC
og_provenance(cad)$clump
##                     id                  ld ld_choice         r2    kb hits
## 1 OGS-00011:GCST003116 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10   matched 0.03186544 10000 2194
##   absent leads
## 1    234    49

hits counts the top hits at the threshold, absent those the LD Store doesn’t hold, and leads the index variants. Two clumpings that differ can be explained from these alone.

Using a PLINK Reference

A PLINK Reference is a PLINK binary genotype fileset (.bed, .bim, .fam) on your own machine, such as the 1000 Genomes files ieugwasr users already have. Pass it as ld to clump or build LD matrices locally with PLINK, as ieugwasr’s local functions did. The Associations can still come from any Source.

ref <- og_plink_reference("~/ld/1kg/EUR")
cad_local <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", ld = ref, r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000)
m_local <- og_ld_matrix(src, cad_local, ld = ref)
# illustrative
ℹ Using PLINK at /usr/local/bin/plink.
ℹ 2,131 of 2,194 top hits matched the PLINK Reference by rsID; 63 not in it were left out.
  • Variants are matched by rsID, because PLINK References are usually on GRCh37 while ALIDs are on GRCh38. Variants without an rsID match are left out, and the message says how many. An LD matrix from a PLINK Reference is named <rsid>_<allele>_<allele> with the PLINK Reference’s alleles, as ieugwasr named it, and the sign of r again refers to the first allele in each name.
  • r2 and kb are required. A PLINK Reference has no recorded defaults, so opengwasr won’t choose for you. Without them, og_tophits() and og_clump() stop and ask for both.
  • PLINK itself is found from og_plink_reference(path, plink_bin = ), then the genetics.binaRies package if it is installed, then your PATH. If none has it, the error says how to install it.
  • og_ld_proxies() reads LD Stores only.
  • Provenance works as before: clump_ld is the PLINK Reference’s path, and clump_ld_choice is "user".

Without an API

With data that already carries rsIDs, og_clump() and og_ld_matrix() with a PLINK Reference need no API at all: pass src = NULL, with no credentials set. If an ALID’s rsID would have to be looked up (no rsid column, and no rsIDs given), they stop with class opengwasr_source_required, which says how many ALIDs need it; pass a Source then.

og_clump(NULL, cad_local, ld = ref, r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000)  # cad_local has an `rsid` column
